books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books.
stimulus.text: Clay's plan first went to the Senate as one large bill, the Omnibus Bill, meant to be voted on all at once. It failed in the Senate in July 1850: Northerners who liked California's admission would not vote for the Fugitive Slave Act, and Southerners who wanted that act would not vote for California. President Zachary Taylor, who opposed the package, died on July 9, 1850, and Millard Fillmore, who favored it, became president. Senator Stephen A. Douglas of Illinois then broke the package into five separate bills, and each one passed with a different mix of Northern and Southern votes. Fillmore signed all five between September 9 and September 20, 1850.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: According to the passage, why did the Omnibus Bill fail in the Senate in July 1850?

options.text: President Fillmore vetoed the Omnibus Bill when it reached his desk.
options.misconception: Fillmore favored the compromise and signed the separate bills; he did not veto the package.

options.text: The Supreme Court declared it unconstitutional.
options.misconception: The courts play no part in the passage; the bill failed on votes, not on a ruling.

options.text: Different groups backed different parts, and none would vote for the whole.
California withdrew its application for statehood and stayed a territory.
options.misconception: California never withdrew its application; its admission was one of the bills that passed.

rationales.A: Fillmore favored the compromise and signed the separate bills; he did not veto the package.
rationales.B: The courts play no part in the passage; the bill failed on votes, not on a ruling.
rationales.C: The passage says Northerners who liked California's admission would not vote for the Fugitive Slave Act, and Southerners who wanted that act would not vote for California.
rationales.D: California never withdrew its application; its admission was one of the bills that passed.
rationales.general:
1. Picture the package as one box holding five different gifts.
2. Background from the books: Northerners wanted California, and Southerners wanted the Fugitive Slave Act.
3. See why the box would not pass: no one would vote for a box holding a gift for the other side.
Remember: a package deal fails when each side loves its own piece and hates the other's.
